extracted.intended_audience: researchers, ERC applicants, panel members, and stakeholders in research funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards describing how the European Research Council organises and conducts peer review for frontier research grants, including panel composition, evaluation stages, scoring, conflicts of interest, and feedback quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence as sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific excellence remains the sole criterion for ERC frontier research grant evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ERC's peer review is designed to identify exceptional proposals across the entire range of scientific disciplines, guided by a focus on scientific excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on project quality and ideas over CV/track record (2024 Work Programme)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2024, the Work Programme introduces changes with a greater emphasis on project quality and the ideas behind a project than an applicant's CV and track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scoring system is adjusted and the CV/track record templates are merged and simplified, allowing applicants to include brief narratives for more clarity so promising proposals are judged primarily on their ideas and project quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merged and simplified CV and track record templates
rubrics_metrics.description: The CV and track record templates are merged and simplified, allowing applicants to include brief narratives for more clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aims to reduce emphasis on long track records and clarify applicants' contributions while supporting the shift toward evaluating project ideas and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring adjustments to protect promising proposals from resubmission restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The scoring system is adjusted to ensure promising proposals are not hindered by resubmission restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes in scoring are intended to avoid penalising applicants due to previous submission history and to allow promising ideas appropriate chances in the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel size and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Each panel is made up of about 15 accomplished, independent researchers, led by a designated chairperson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels convene to perform a comprehensive two-stage evaluation for ERC grants for individual researchers; the chairperson leads panel deliberations and organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel member selection criteria and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of panel members is meticulously overseen by the ERC Scientific Council, with emphasis on their scientific standing and based on criteria set by the ERC Scientific Council Standing Committee on Panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This selection process underscores the ERC's dedication to professionalism in panel member selection and to achieving expertise balance within each panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise balance and coverage, including emerging trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels should have a well-rounded expertise coverage so that emerging scientific trends in submissions are appropriately covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific Officers continually assess the need for expertise coverage in panels to ensure proposals are treated fairly and impartially and that relevant fields and emerging topics are represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage evaluation process (panel and final phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ERC individual grants, each panel convenes twice for a comprehensive two-stage evaluation: an initial stage where panel members adopt a generalist perspective assessing proposals broadly, followed by a second/final phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first stage emphasises broad assessment (generalist perspective) informed by members' expertise; the second stage involves external expert assessments and interviews and culminates in panel discussion to make final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent external experts (remote reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent external experts are engaged to assess the highest-ranked proposals; these external assessments are used in the panel discussions during the second and final phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External reviewers' reports inform panel questions and deliberations and are considered alongside panel members' expertise to ensure rigorous assessment of top proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant interviews in final evaluation phase
rubrics_metrics.description: During the final phase, panel members conduct interviews with applicants, framing inquiries and conveying questions based on their own expertise and the reviews provided by the external experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews allow panels to probe proposal details, clarify reviewers' concerns, and assess applicants' ability to carry out the proposed research informed by both panel and external reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and constructiveness of feedback to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: High quality, constructive feedback is a priority and can profoundly influence applicants' decisions regarding potential reapplication and proposal improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Scientific Council remains unwavering in ensuring high quality throughout the process, particularly in the feedback provided to applicants; applicants often place importance on this feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules to avoid geographic and institutional bias in panels
rubrics_metrics.description: There are established rules to avoid that panels have biased geographical and institutional memberships: no more than two members are from the same country and no more than one member can come from a specific institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules help ensure impartiality and diversity of perspectives across panels and reduce concentration of influence from particular countries or institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel member participation and eligibility/conflict rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear rules govern panel member participation and eligibility to apply: panel members can serve in alternating years for up to four terms and are not allowed to apply for an ERC grant in the same year and panel that they serve as panel members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions are in place to uphold fairness and impartiality and to prevent potential conflicts of interest in the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality, transparency and professionalism in the selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERC places the utmost importance on impartiality and transparency in the selection process, aiming for a peer-review system respected in the scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall governance (Scientific Council oversight, Standing Committee on Panels, Scientific Officers' support, and membership rules) is organised to maintain professionalism, impartiality and transparency across the evaluation process.
